questions.question:
Which of the following reagents/reactions will convert 'A' to 'B'?
 

1. PCC oxidation
2. Ozonolysis
3. \( \text{BH}_3,\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/^-\text{OH}\) followed by PCC oxidation
4. HBr, hydrolysis followed by oxidation by \(\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7.\)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Apply anti-Markovnikov's rule when peroxide is given. Explanation: (1) PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate) is a mild oxidizing agent used for the oxidation of primary alcohols to aldehydes and secondary alcohols to ketones. It does not directly react with alkenes to form aldehydes. (2) Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond of alkenes and forms carbonyl compounds, followed by reductive workup (e.g., with Zn/H₂O or Me₂S). In this case, ozonolysis of compound A would cleave the double bond, forming formaldehyde (HCHO) and a ketone, not the desired aldehyde.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ (3) Hydroboration-oxidation reaction adds water across the double bond in an anti-Markovnikov fashion, resulting in the formation of a primary alcohol. In this case, it would convert the exocyclic alkene to a primary alcohol. Subsequent PCC oxidation of the primary alcohol (CH₂OH) would convert it into an aldehyde (CHO). (4) HBr would add across the double bond according to Markovnikov's rule, placing the bromine on the more substituted carbon. Subsequent hydrolysis would replace the bromine with a hydroxyl group, forming a tertiary alcohol. Tertiary alcohols cannot be oxidized under these conditions. The reagent used to convert A into B are given as follows: The first step involves addition of\(\text{H}_2\text{O}\)to alkene according to anti-markownikoff’s rule, while the second step involves oxidation of \(1^\circ\) alcohol to aldehyde. Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

Match the following compounds in List-I with their corresponding \(\mathrm{pK_a}\)​ values in List-II.
List-I (Compounds)List-II (\(\mathrm{pK_a}\))
(a)p-Nitrophenol(i)10
(b)m-Nitrophenol(ii)16
(c)Ethanol(iii)7.1
(d)Phenol(iv)8.3
1. (a)→(i); (b)→(ii); (c)→(iii); (d)→(iv)
2. (a)→(iii); (b)→(iv); (c)→(ii); (d)→(i)
3. (a)→(iv); (b)→(iii); (c)→(ii); (d)→(i)
4. (a)→(iii); (b)→(iv); (c)→(i); (d)→(ii)
questions.explanation:
Hint: Electron-withdrawing nitro groups lower pKa. Explanation:Solution: Acid strength is inversely proportional to pKₐ. Lower pKₐ means stronger acid. Step 1: p-Nitrophenol The para-NO₂ group stabilizes the phenoxide ion through both −I and −M effects. pKₐ ≈ 7.1 Step 2: m-Nitrophenol At the meta position, the nitro group stabilizes the phenoxide ion mainly through the −I effect, rather than direct resonance interaction with the negative charge. pKₐ ≈ 8.3 Step 3: Phenol The phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance. pKₐ ≈ 10 Step 4: Ethanol Ethoxide ion does not receive resonance stabilization. pKₐ ≈ 16 Therefore, the decreasing order of acidity is: p-Nitrophenol > m-Nitrophenol > Phenol > Ethanol Hence, option 2nd is the correct answer.
